inspector.redacted: Tokens, codes, cookies and keys in this message were replaced by placeholders.

stepHelp.issuerOffer: The issuer creates a credential offer: which credential the wallet may collect and a one-time pre-authorized code. A wallet receives it as a QR code or link, or the playground hands it to the wallet directly.
stepHelp.issuerMetadata: The wallet downloads the issuer’s metadata to learn the credential endpoint, the credential types and formats on offer, and which proof of key possession the issuer accepts.
stepHelp.asMetadata: The wallet looks up the authorization server that issues access tokens for this issuer, and its token endpoint.
stepHelp.token: The wallet trades the pre-authorized code (or an authorization code) for an access token. The answer may carry a c_nonce that the wallet must sign in its proof.
stepHelp.nonce: The wallet asks the issuer for a fresh nonce, so the proof of possession it signs next cannot be replayed.
stepHelp.credential: The wallet sends a JWT signed with its own key (the proof of possession) and receives the signed credential, bound to that key.
stepHelp.verifierRequest: The verifier creates an authorization request saying which credential and which claims it needs: a Presentation Exchange definition or a DCQL query, plus a nonce and where to send the answer.
stepHelp.walletFetchRequest: The wallet downloads the request object the authorization request points to (request_uri). It is usually a signed JWT carrying the query, the nonce and the response URI.
stepHelp.walletSubmit: The wallet posts its answer to the verifier’s response URI: the vp_token (the presentation, signed with the holder’s key over the verifier’s nonce) and, with Presentation Exchange, the presentation_submission that maps it to the request.
stepHelp.verifierResult: The verifier checks the issuer’s signature, the dates, the holder binding (nonce and audience) and the disclosed claims, then reports its result.
stepHelp.personAction: A person has to act: scan a QR code with a phone wallet or open a link. The run continues when the server sees the wallet’s request.
stepHelp.playgroundAdmin: A set-up call the playground makes to a role before the protocol starts, for example asking an issuer to prepare an offer. It is not part of the standard.

about.title: About the playground
about.what: The playground runs one verifiable-credential flow at a time: an issuer issues a credential to a wallet, the wallet presents it to a verifier, and the verifier checks it. Each role can be an Inji module or a reference implementation written independently from the published standards.
about.capture: Every HTTP request between the roles passes through the playground server, which records it. The timeline and the inspector show those recorded messages, never prepared examples.
